prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks are an exceptionally clean case of a foundational measurement platform made physically real: confinement at the magic wavelength addresses a central limitation of atomic clocks while preserving exquisite quantum control. The achievement is mature, reproducible in independent laboratories, and already enables precision tests rather than resting on prospective applications. Katori and Ye provide an unusually clear, complementary attribution to the central concept and its decisive realization.
statement.case_against: The most visible consequences remain metrological, and the eventual redefinition of the second is not itself a criterion of scientific merit. Circuit QED has, in my view, an equally profound claim as a newly controllable quantum regime, but its separation from superconducting-circuit advances recognized in 2025 requires a sharper historical boundary.

responses.point: Kroll places B052 first, emphasizing the clear division between Katori's magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and Ye's experimental development, while noting the attribution difficulty and overlap with the broader superconducting-qubit enterprise for B036.
responses.response: I agree that the lattice-clock attribution is unusually well delimited and that its independent reproduction establishes maturity beyond doubt. I also share the qualification on B036: circuit QED is not merely an application, but we must establish that its distinctive light-matter physics can be separated fairly from the superconducting-circuit work already rewarded.

responses.point: Lindroth identifies B052 as a lasting fundamental advance in precision measurement and regards Katori and Ye as its central pioneers.
responses.response: That assessment has moved B052 above my initial preference. Its value is not only better clocks: it demonstrates controlled many-atom quantum systems at a precision that makes new gravitational and fundamental-physics measurements credible. I would nevertheless avoid making future applications or standards-policy decisions part of the citation.

uncertainties: Whether the historical record supports treating circuit QED as sufficiently distinct from the superconducting-circuit achievement recognized in 2025.
Whether all essential early optical-lattice-clock contributions are adequately represented by the two credited names.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
